name: Earned Income Tax Credit
valueBasis: A refundable credit: the phase-in rate times earned income, capped at the maximum for the number of qualifying children, less the phase-out.

criteria.instructions: Does anyone in this household have earned income — wages, salary, tips or self-employment? Social Security, unemployment and other benefits are not earned income.
criteria.askIfUnsure: Did anyone in your household work for pay during the year?
criteria.note: Without earned income the credit is zero regardless of everything else. IRC 32(a).

criteria.instructions: What filing status would this person use?
criteria.askIfUnsure: On your taxes, do you file single, head of household, or married filing jointly?
criteria.note: Married filing jointly has a higher phase-out threshold in every bracket.

criteria.instructions: This person is married and not filing jointly. Do they meet the separated-spouse rules: legally separated under a written agreement or decree, or living apart from their spouse for the last six months of the year, with a qualifying child living with them for more than half the year?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Have you lived apart from your spouse since at least the middle of the year, with your child living with you?
criteria.note: A married claimant filing separately is not barred outright. IRC 32(d) admits one who meets these rules, and the revenue procedures apply the non-joint thresholds to them.

criteria.instructions: Does this person have investment income — interest, dividends, capital gains, rental income — above the annual limit?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Did you earn more than about twelve thousand dollars from savings, investments or rent?
criteria.note: A cliff rather than a phase-out: one dollar over forfeits the entire credit. IRC 32(i).

criteria.instructions: Does the claimant have a Social Security number valid for employment?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Do you have a Social Security number that lets you work?

criteria.instructions: Would this person file Form 2555 for foreign earned income?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Did you live and work outside the United States this year?

criteria.instructions: Could this person be claimed as a dependent or qualifying child on someone else's return?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Does anyone else claim you on their tax return?
criteria.note: Applies to a claimant with no qualifying children. IRC 32(c)(1)(A)(ii).

criteria.instructions: Is this child the claimant's son, daughter, stepchild, foster child, brother, sister, half-sibling, step-sibling, or a descendant of any of them?
criteria.askIfUnsure: How is this child related to you?

criteria.instructions: Is this child under 19 at the end of the year, or under 24 and a full-time student, or permanently and totally disabled at any age?
criteria.askIfUnsure: How old is this child, and are they a full-time student?

criteria.instructions: Did this child live with the claimant in the United States for more than half of the year?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Did this child live with you for more than six months of the year?

criteria.true: yes, more than half the year

criteria.note: The test most often failed in shared-custody arrangements. IRC 152(c)(1)(B).

criteria.instructions: Did this child file a joint return for the year, other than solely to claim a refund?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Is this child married and filing taxes jointly?

criteria.instructions: Is this child claimed for the EITC on another person's return for the same year?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Does the child's other parent claim them on their taxes?
criteria.note: Only one person may claim a given child. IRC 32(c)(1)(C).

criteria.instructions: How old is the claimant? This matters only when there are no qualifying children.
criteria.note: A claimant with no qualifying children must be at least 25 and under 65 at the end of the year. On a joint return only one spouse need meet it.

verdict: has_earned_income AND valid_ssn AND NOT investment_income_over_limit AND income_limit_test AND credit_above_zero
